image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a surface. The organism displays an elongated oval shape with a distinct dorsal armor consisting of eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in a linear series. These plates are greyish-green with vertical striations and dark central markings. The plates are surrounded by a thick, textured, brownish leathery girdle (mantle) that forms the outer boundary of the body. The head region is indistinct and blunt, lacking visible eyes or tentacles.
